question: Who was the author of the literary work 'Ratnavali'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshavardhana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harshavardhana** was the author of the literary work 'Ratnavali'.
 
• Harshavardhana, also known as Harsha, was an Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE.
 
• He was a patron of arts and literature, and his court was adorned with scholars such as Banabhatta and Mayura.
 
• Harsha himself wrote three Sanskrit plays: 'Nagananda', 'Ratnavali', and 'Priyadarsika'.
 
• 'Ratnavali' is a significant work in the realm of classical Sanskrit literature and reflects Harsha's literary prowess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana** was a ruler from the Vardhana dynasty and was known for his administrative capabilities and military conquests.
 
• He shifted his capital from Thanesar to Kannauj and ruled over a vast territory including parts of present-day Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar.
 
• Harsha's reign is often considered a period of peace and prosperity, and he is remembered for his contributions to culture and religion.
 
• He was a devotee of Buddhism and organized the Kanauj Assembly and the Prayag Assembly to discuss religious matters.
 
• His biography, 'Harshacharita', was written by the court poet Banabhatta and provides a detailed account of his life and times.
